# Overview {-}

Clustering is often followed by a test of whether two of the estimated clusters have
different means. If the same data are used both to form the clusters and to test them,
a classical two-sample test, such as Hotelling's $T^2$ test, rejects true null hypotheses
far more often than its nominal level: the clustering algorithm has already chosen groups
that look different.

**selectiveHotelling** computes *selective* $p$-values, which account for the fact that
the clusters were estimated from the data. A test based on these $p$-values rejects a
true null hypothesis with probability at most $\alpha$ among the data sets on which the
clustering returns the tested clusters. Unlike earlier selective tests for clustering,
the tests in this package do not need the covariance matrix of the features: it can be
**unknown and unstructured**.

The tests work with any clustering algorithm. This tutorial covers

- $k$-means clustering (Chapter \@ref(kmeans)),
- hierarchical clustering (Chapter \@ref(hclust)),
- any other clustering algorithm (Chapter \@ref(any)),
- a faster one-dimensional test (Chapter \@ref(onedim)),
- a real data example (Chapter \@ref(realdata)), and
- the ideas behind the tests and practical advice (Chapter \@ref(details)).

## Installation {-}

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("yiqunchen/selectiveHotelling")
```

The package depends only on base R. This tutorial also uses the **palmerpenguins** data in
Chapter \@ref(realdata).
